title: Vegan Salvadoran Classics Tasted: Pastelitos and Yuca Frita Reimagined with Jackfruit and Impossible Meat
summary: In this Goodful video, a host pairs Salvadoran dishes with vegan substitutions and invites family members to taste-test pastelitos and yuca frita. The host explains that jackfruit stands in for chicharrón and Impossible Meat substitutes for ground beef, framing the meal as a playful challenge to see if the family can identify the traditional dish when it’s vegan. Throughout the tasting, the family provides enthusiastic reactions, comments on authenticity tied to heritage (including references to grandma’s recipe and “herencia”), and participates in a brief tutorial on what vegan means. The segment blends cultural foodways with plant-based cooking, capturing moments of tradition, discovery, and potential expansion of vegan Latin American fare.
topics: Impossible Meat as ground beef substitute
Texture and mouthfeel of vegan fillings
Eating with hands vs utensils in traditional dishes
Herencia and cultural authenticity in cooking

sections.title: Second dish and heritage discussion
sections.description: The second dish is presented as a vegan take on a traditional favorite. Family members reference lineage and older recipes, framing the vegan remake as an extension of family heritage rather than a replacement.

sections.title: What is vegan? Explanations and reactions
sections.description: A brief educational moment clarifies what vegan means for the audience, including how the meat substitute relates to traditional flavors. The family expresses ongoing interest and openness to trying more vegan Latin American dishes.

sections.title: Closing thoughts and future plans
concepts: Encouragement to make more vegan Latin American dishes
